description: Search the text of all the law in force on a date, across every jurisdiction or one, in the law's own language. Plain words are a phrase; when no provision holds the phrase, the provisions that hold all the words are given. Names the acts that match best. The answer also describes the first provisions found (matches): for each, how to cite it, its official page, what last changed it and an excerpt. An excerpt is part of a provision, not the whole: read_law gives the whole.

case_sensitive.description: Match upper and lower case as written (default false: either case matches).

date.description: An in-force date, YYYY-MM-DD, or "today". Defaults to today.

jurisdiction.description: Optional jurisdiction: a country by its name in English or its own language ("germany", "Deutschland", "UK") or its ISO code ("de"), or a path prefix, for example "germany", "united-states/federal" or "united-kingdom/uk/legislation/uksi".

kind.description: laws (default; "law" is read the same): law only. judgments: court decisions (case law) only. all: both. A jurisdiction that names case law (a path ending in /caselaw) reads it too.

max_results.description: Matching lines to return (default 30, at most 200).

offset.description: Rows to skip: the next_offset the answer before gave in "page" (default 0).

order.description: relevance (default): within each body of law, the provisions in which the words occur most come first, each with its first three matching lines, where the server can rank them. path: every matching line, in the order of the files' names.

query.description: Words or a phrase; a regular expression if regex is true.

regex.description: Read query as a regular expression (POSIX extended, as git grep -E reads it) instead of plain text (default false).

name: search_law
title: Search law
